item.title: Court-declared mayor Shahadat now appointed Chattogram City administrator
item.description:
The government has appointed ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Shahadat Hossain, who became mayor of Chattogram City Corporation following a court ruling, as the administrator of the same corporation.

He was appointed on a full-time basis through a notification issued by the Local Government Division on Sunday (25 October).

The Local Government Division had prepared a proposal to appoint Shahadat Hossain as administrator in March as well, but no order was issued at the time. He has now been appointed administrator amid questions over the tenure of the elected council and his continuation in the mayoral office.

The notification, signed by Local Government Division Deputy Secretary Jewel Rana, states that Shahadat Hossain will serve as administrator until further orders under Section 4 of the Local Government (City Corporation) (Amendment) Act, 2026.

According to the notification, he will receive monthly remuneration and other allowances in accordance with the rules. The order, issued in the public interest, takes immediate effect.

Questions over tenure; previous move to appoint him administrator

On 27 April, Prothom Alo ran a report on the tenure of Chattogram City Corporation’s elected council and Shahadat Hossain’s continuation in office. Citing documents from the Local Government Division, the report said the elected council held its first meeting on 23 February 2021. Accordingly, its five-year term ended on 22 February this year.

Shahadat Hossain, however, had told Prothom Alo at the time that, under a court order, his tenure would continue until November 2029. However, documents from the Local Government Division stated that although the court had declared him mayor, it had issued no separate direction regarding the length of his tenure.

According to the report, a proposal to appoint Shahadat as a full-time administrator had been prepared in March, but no order was issued. Earlier, on 3 February, the Local Government Division had written to the election commission requesting that arrangements be made to hold an election.

How Shahadat became mayor

BNP leader Shahadat Hossain contested the mayoral election of Chattogram City Corporation held on 27 January 2021. According to the results announced at the time, Awami League candidate Rezaul Karim Chowdhury was declared the winner with 369,248 votes. Shahadat Hossain, his closest rival, was shown to have received 52,489 votes.

Alleging widespread irregularities and vote-rigging, Shahadat filed a case with the election tribunal on 24 February that year, seeking to have the results annulled. Nine people, including the then chief election commissioner, were named as defendants.

Following the fall of the Awami League government on 5 August 2024, Rezaul Karim Chowdhury was removed from the mayoral post. On 19 August that year, the government appointed Chattogram Divisional Commissioner Md Tofail Islam as administrator of the city corporation.

Subsequently, on 1 October, Mohammad Khairul Amin, judge of the Chattogram election tribunal and joint district and sessions judge, delivered a verdict in Shahadat’s case. The ruling overturned the decision to declare Rezaul Karim Chowdhury elected and declared Shahadat Hossain the elected mayor. It also directed that a notification be issued to this effect within 10 days.

Following the court’s order, the election commission issued a revised notification on 8 October, declaring Shahadat Hossain mayor. He was sworn in on 3 November in the conference room of the Local Government Division at the Secretariat. AF Hassan Ariff, the then local government adviser to the interim government, administered the oath.

Nearly three years and nine months after the election, Shahadat was sworn in as mayor. He will now run the corporation as an administrator appointed by the government.

item.title: Saint Martin’s Island to reopen to tourists on 1 November
item.description:
Saint Martin’s Island, one of the country’s most popular tourist destinations, is set to reopen to visitors on 1 November after remaining closed for nearly 10 months.

Tourist travel to Saint Martin’s Island will continue until 15 March next year. A maximum of 3,500 tourists will be allowed to visit the island each day, with each visitor required to pay an environmental conservation fee of Tk 100.

The decisions on tourist access to the ecologically critical Saint Martin’s Island were taken at an interministerial meeting held at the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change on 12 October. On Sunday, the ministry’s Environment-2 wing issued directives to the relevant ministries and departments to implement the decisions.

The directives state that the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA) and the Department of Shipping cannot permit vessels to operate to Saint Martin’s Island without approval from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

Approved tourist vessels will continue operating from the Nuniyachhara jetty.

The Department of Environment has been instructed to take the necessary measures to collect the environmental conservation fee in accordance with Rule 26 of the Environment Conservation Area Management Rules, 2016. The directives issued in a notification by the Environment Ministry on 22 October 2025 will also remain in force.

The notification instructs the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism, the Ministry of Shipping, the Department of Environment, the Cox’s Bazar district administration and other relevant agencies to take the necessary steps to implement the decisions on tourist access to the ecologically critical island.

During the interim government’s tenure, access to Saint Martin’s Island was restricted to protect the environment. Although the island was opened to tourists on 1 November last year, visitors could not travel there that month because vessel operations remained suspended. Overnight stays were also prohibited in November. Tourists were allowed to stay overnight in December and January, with a daily limit of 2,000 visitors permitted to visit and spend the night on the island.

Four years ago, five to six thousand tourists travelled to Saint Martin’s Island every day on nine to 11 vessels departing from Teknaf. They reached the island after crossing the 13-kilometre Naf River and travelling across 21 kilometres of the Bay of Bengal.

However, vessel operations on the Teknaf–Saint Martin’s route were suspended amid several developments, including the conflict in Myanmar’s Rakhine State, the Arakan Army’s takeover of territory in the state, gunfire targeting Bangladeshi trawlers and passenger vessels operating on the Naf River, and the abduction of Bangladeshi nationals along with their boats.

item.title: Jamaat’s district leadership: The same faces hold top posts for years
item.description:
Syed Md Abdul Momen, ameer of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami’s Khagrachhari district unit, has held the post for nearly 28 years at a stretch, since 1998. Jamaat has 79 organisational units across the country at district and city levels.

Prothom Alo examined 43 of these units and found that, as in Khagrachhari, the same person has served as the top leader in many units for years.

Information collected from Jamaat leaders and Prothom Alo’s district correspondents shows that 19 units have had no change in the post of ameer for 10 years or more.

In another 11 units, the same person has held the post for between five and nine years. In one district, a leader has served as ameer for a total of 22 years, with a break in between.

On 14 October, crude bomb explosions and vandalism took place on the premises of Jamaat-e-Islami’s Cumilla city office over the formation of a committee. The personal car of Mahbubur Rahman, secretary of the city Jamaat unit, was also vandalised.

Responsible sources within Jamaat say there has been discussion within the party about the same individuals holding top positions for extended periods.

Kazi Din Mohammad served as ameer of Cumilla city Jamaat for 28 years. Following the clashes over the committee, he was relieved of his post on 16 October, and the committee was dissolved.

Some party members see the incident in Cumilla as an expression of simmering discontent within Jamaat’s organisational politics.

Following the incident, a former publicity secretary of a Jamaat unit from another district wrote on Facebook, “Allah knows how far the ‘Lu’ wind from ‘Ku’ will spread. It is important to take the discontent of subordinates seriously at the centre.”

Some within Jamaat have also questioned whether the party is failing to develop new leaders or whether a section of its long-serving leaders are clinging to their positions.

Responsible sources within Jamaat say there has been discussion within the party about the same individuals holding top positions for extended periods.

Jamaat to investigate what lies behind incident in Cumilla
Speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, several Jamaat leaders said many full-timers tended to cling to their positions. District and city ameers are also given priority when the party nominates candidates for national parliamentary elections.

According to Jamaat-e-Islami’s constitution, the central committee and the post of ameer have a term of three years, while district and city committees serve two-year terms. In both cases, the ameer is elected by secret ballot among the party’s rukons (members).

Jamaat therefore describes its leadership selection process as “fully democratic”. However, the party does not disclose detailed information about the number of voters, the votes received by candidates or the level of competition.

As a result, it remains unclear why the same individuals have continued to lead for so long and how effectively the leadership selection process fosters competition.

Full-time party workers

It is nothing new for the same person to hold a top position for many years in Bangladesh’s mainstream political parties. However, other positions below the top leadership tend to change hands in those parties.

In Jamaat-e-Islami, however, there are also instances of the same person holding the second-highest position for an extended period.

According to Jamaat’s internal sources, Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan has served as district ameer in Lakshmipur for 23 years, Hafizur Rahman in Jhalakathi for 22 years and Fazlur Rahman Sayeed in Joypurhat for 20 years.

According to sources within Jamaat, the party covers the expenses of senior leaders on the central committee as well as district and city committees who devote themselves to party work full-time.

In some cases, they are provided with cars and other necessary facilities. They are known within Jamaat as “full-timers” (salaried party workers). Some full-timers are appointed to senior positions in institutions run with party funding, where they receive salaries.

Speaking to Prothom Alo on condition of anonymity, several Jamaat leaders said many full-timers tended to cling to their positions.

District and city ameers are also given priority when the party nominates candidates for national parliamentary elections. This, too, has encouraged them to hold on to top positions, limiting opportunities for newcomers to take up leadership roles.

Central Jamaat leaders, however, are reluctant to accept these allegations. They maintain that ameers are elected on the basis of their qualifications, organisational skills and dedication to the Islamic movement, and that personal ambitions or expectations are not the deciding factors.

Muhammad Shahjahan, Jamaat’s regional director for ChattogramLeadership passes to those whom district ameers groom as leaders. Therefore, it is not true that new leaders are not emerging.

Muazzam Hossain Helal, Jamaat’s regional director for Barishal, described the process of electing leaders in different party units as “democratic”.

Speaking to Prothom Alo, he said rukons (oath-taking party members) elect the ameer by voting for their preferred candidate. He added that the party also removes people from their positions when it deems necessary.

Districts where same faces served for years

According to Jamaat’s internal sources, Ruhul Amin Bhuiyan has served as district ameer in Lakshmipur for 23 years, Hafizur Rahman in Jhalakathi for 22 years and Fazlur Rahman Sayeed in Joypurhat for 20 years.

Nurul Islam became Rajbari district ameer in 2009. Before that, he served as acting ameer for two years and district secretary for three years. Altogether, he has held the post of ameer for 19 years.

Emran Hossain, ameer of Jamaat’s Khulna district unit, has held the same position for 18 years, while Abdul Jabbar in Barishal has served for 17 years. SM Abdus Salam Azad in Bandarban and Abdul Alim in Rangamati have each been district amer for 16 years.

Before the 13th national parliamentary election, Jamaat’s ameer said at a reception for elected student union representatives on 7 November 2025, “The young will sit in the cockpit and run the country. We will provide support from behind.”

Shahinur Alam in Sirajganj has held the post for 14 years, while Jahangir Alam in Gazipur has served for 13 years. The same individuals have been ameers of the district and city units in Bogura and Mmensingh for 11 years.

The current ameers in Tangail, Meherpur and Pabna are completing their 10th year in office.

Mohammad Azizur Rahman of Kurigram served as ameer for 22 years at a stretch, from 1996 to 2018. He was principal of Bhurungamari Degree College, now Bhurungamari Government College.

He stepped down as ameer when the issue of nationalising the college came to the fore. In December last year, he was appointed district ameer again.

Five district ameers became members of parliament after being nominated by Jamaat in the 13th national parliamentary election.

They are Ataur Rahman of Narail, Mohammad Ruhul Amin of Chuadanga, Mohammad Tajuddin Khan of Meherpur, Ali Azam Mohammad Abubakar of Jhenaidah and Professor Abu Taleb Mondal of Pabna.

Sources within Jamaat say defying party decisions and engaging in clashes over positions could emerge as new challenges for the party in the coming days. This is why the party has taken the incident in Cumilla seriously.

Before the 13th national parliamentary election, Jamaat’s ameer said at a reception for elected student union representatives on 7 November 2025, “The young will sit in the cockpit and run the country. We will provide support from behind.”

However, some former leaders of Islami Chhatra Shibir believe that young people are not advancing into leadership as they should because many Jamaat leaders at the district level tend to cling to their positions.

Muhammad Shahjahan, Jamaat’s regional director for Chattogram, told Prothom Alo that leadership passes to those whom district ameers groom as leaders. Therefore, he said, it is not true that new leaders are not emerging.

Pressure mounts after becoming main opposition

With 76 seats in the current parliament, Jamaat-e-Islami has taken its place as the main opposition party. This marks the party’s greatest success in parliamentary politics.

Its influence and political activities have grown since 2024 mass uprising, and it has attracted new leaders and supporters. Among them is former BNP MP Akhtaruzzaman, who joined Jamaat.

Jamaat’s senior leaders often describe it as a disciplined organisation whose leaders and activists do not act against the central leadership’s directives. However, after the party announced its candidate for the Cumilla-7 (Chandina) constituency in the last parliamentary election, local activists expressed anger. Supporters of the two sides were also involved in scuffles and clashes.

Party leaders believe that, overall, internal competition for positions and influence has also intensified.

On 12 October, Ahad Ali, president of Jamaat’s youth wing at the union level, announced his candidacy for chairman of the Uthali Union Parishad in Jibannagar upazila of Chuadanga, going against the party’s decision.

Ahad Ali declared his candidacy in defiance of the party after it nominated another candidate. He was later expelled from the party.

Jamaat’s senior leaders often describe it as a disciplined organisation whose leaders and activists do not act against the central leadership’s directives.

However, after the party announced its candidate for the Cumilla-7 (Chandina) constituency in the last parliamentary election, local activists expressed anger. Supporters of the two sides were also involved in scuffles and clashes.

Jamaat discusses advisory council; ex-bureaucrats, academics, businesspeople may join

In the last election, Golam Sarwar, also known as Sarwar Tushar, joint convener of the National Citizen Party (NCP), was named the candidate of the 11-party alliance led by Jamaat for the Narsingdi-2 constituency.

However, Jamaat leader Amjad Hossain contested the election going against the decisions of both his party and the alliance.

Jamaat had also ceded the Chattogram-8 constituency to NCP’s Jubairul Hasan, the candidate of the 11-party alliance. However, Jamaat’s Abu Naser neither withdrew his nomination papers nor stepped aside from the election.

Sources within Jamaat say defying party decisions and engaging in clashes over positions could emerge as new challenges for the party in the coming days. This is why the party has taken the incident in Cumilla seriously.

However, Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Abdul Halim believes that an incident like the one in Cumilla will not happen anywhere else.

item.title: Witness in Sayedee case buried late at night after tension over guard of honour
item.description:
Freedom fighter Manik Pashari, 87, who testified against former Jamaat-e-Islami leader Delwar Hossain Sayedee before the International Crimes Tribunal in a crimes against humanity case over atrocities committed in 1971, has been buried.

Radheshyam Sarkar, officer-in-charge (investigation) of Pirojpur Sadar Police Station, said Manik Pashari was buried at around 1:30 am on Sunday in the family graveyard at his home in Chitolia village of Pirojpur Sadar upazila. Family members and relatives were present at the burial.

Tension erupted in Pirojpur on Saturday over the decision to accord Manik Pashari a guard of honour. Some local people demanded that he not be buried there.

During the ensuing tensions, Jamaat-e-Islami leaders and activists were seen gathering and taking positions at various key locations in Pirojpur town.

However, Zahirul Haque, secretary of Pirojpur district Jamaat-e-Islami, said, “We had no objection to Manik Pashari’s burial. However, we did not provide any assistance either. We know nothing about under whose patronage and with whose assistance from the administration the burial took place.”

Manik Pashari was a resident of Chitolia village in Pirojpur Sadar upazila.

According to his family members, he had been staying at his son-in-law’s house in Tungipara, Gopalganj, since 5 August 2024. After being ill for two months, he died there at around 10 am on Saturday.

According to police sources, his relatives brought his body to the Pirojpur Sadar Upazila Parishad around noon on Saturday. The body was subsequently taken to the Pirojpur Police Lines, where he was accorded a guard of honour. He was buried at around 1:30 am on Sunday.

Delwar Hossain Sayedee was sentenced to imprisonment until death in a crimes against humanity case relating to the 1971 Liberation War. He died on the night of 14 August 2023 while undergoing treatment in prison custody.

item.title: No party candidate announced for DSCC: State Minister for Local Govt
Monira removed from leadership of NCP’s women’s wing, Mahmuda -Nusrat ‘promoted’
item.description:
The National Citizen Party’s (NCP) women’s wing, Jatiya Nari Shakti, has dissolved its central committee and announced a new one, seven and a half months after the organisation’s launch.

The changes have effectively removed Monira Sharmin from the organisation’s top leadership. The party has replaced her as convener with NCP Member of Parliament Mahmuda Alam Mitu, who previously served as member secretary.

Nusrat Tabassum, who previously held the position of chief organiser, the third-highest post, has become the new member secretary.

The NCP published a new, partially formed three-member committee of Nari Shakti on its verified Facebook page shortly after 12:15 pm on Sunday. The committee names Mahmuda and Nusrat, both NCP MPs elected to reserved seats for women, alongside Monjila Jhuma, who will serve as the organisation’s chief organiser.

Jatiya Nari Shakti was launched on 8 March, International Women’s Day. Initially, the party named Monira as convener, Mahmuda as member secretary and Nusrat as chief organiser.

On 18 April, the organisation announced its full 53-member committee. The party has now dissolved that committee.

A notice on the decision stated that NCP Convener Md Nahid Islam and Member Secretary Akhter Hossain had directed the party to cancel the existing Jatiya Nari Shakti committee and approve a new, partially formed convening committee. It also instructed the new committee to announce its full membership within the next 15 days.

In April, the NCP initially finalised Monira and Mahmuda as its candidates for reserved women’s seats in the 13th national parliamentary election. However, the Election Commission (EC) rejected Monira’s nomination papers during scrutiny.

Nusrat had also submitted nomination papers for a reserved seat. The EC initially refused to accept her papers because she attempted to submit them after the deadline. The commission later accepted her nomination following a court order. She ultimately became an MP.

item.title: Infinix launches NOTE 60 Ultra with Ferrari-linked design heritage
item.description:
Global smartphone brand Infinix has launched the NOTE 60 Ultra in Bangladesh, introducing a new addition to its NOTE 60 Series, reports a press release.

Developed in collaboration with Italian design house Pininfarina, known for its work with Ferrari and Alfa Romeo, the smartphone combines automotive-inspired design with a MediaTek Dimensity 8400 Ultimate 5G chipset, a 200MP camera system and a 7,000mAh battery.

The company has also introduced the NOTE 60 Pro Torino Black Special Edition.

The NOTE 60 Ultra features a Uni-Chassis camera module inspired by the bodywork of sports cars.

The design integrates three cameras, an Active-Matrix display and rear lighting beneath a single glass panel, creating a seamless appearance. A rear light inspired by supercar taillights illuminates during startup and notifications.

The phone also features a matte aluminium alloy frame, rounded edges and a racing-inspired user interface. It comes in four colours: Monza Red, Torino Black, Amalfi Blue and Roma Silver.

The smartphone is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 8400 Ultimate 5G chipset, paired with 12GB LPDDR5X RAM and 512GB UFS 4.0 internal storage for faster data transfer, responsive multitasking and smooth gaming performance.

According to Infinix, the device records an AnTuTu benchmark score of over 2.09 million. A 3D IceCore Cooling System helps manage heat during extended use.

The phone also features a 1.5K display with a refresh rate of up to 144Hz, peak brightness of 4,500 nits and JBL-tuned dual stereo speakers.

For photography, the NOTE 60 Ultra comes with a 200MP Samsung ISOCELL HPE main camera and a 50MP periscope telephoto camera, supporting 3.5x optical zoom and up to 100x digital zoom. It also offers Ultra HDR photography, 4K video recording at 60fps and a 32MP front camera.

The device packs a 7,000mAh silicon-carbon battery with 100W wired and 50W wireless charging.

According to Infinix's laboratory tests, the battery can reach 50 per cent charge in approximately 18 minutes.

Battery Self-Healing Technology and Bypass Charging are also included to help maintain battery performance and manage heat during intensive use.

Alongside the Ultra, Infinix has launched the NOTE 60 Pro Torino Black Special Edition, featuring a Kevlar-pattern finish, racing-inspired software, an exclusive Pininfarina watermark and a co-branded gift box with customised accessories.

The special edition is powered by the Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 5G chipset and features a 50MP OIS main camera, a 1.5K 144Hz display, an interactive Active-Matrix display and JBL-tuned stereo speakers. It supports 90W wired and 30W wireless charging.

The Infinix NOTE 60 Ultra is priced at Tk 99,999. For consumers looking for a more accessible option, the NOTE 60 Pro, including the Pininfarina-inspired Torino Black Special Edition, is available at Tk 45,999 after a Tk 4,000 discount.

The NOTE 60 is also available at Tk 37,999 with Tk 7,000 cashback, giving consumers additional savings on selected models in the NOTE 60 Series.

item.title: Cyberattack fears: Janata Bank, Bengal Commercial Bank websites go offline
item.description:
The websites of Janata Bank and Bengal Commercial Bank have been shut down amid fears of cyberattacks. Users are unable to access either website, leaving customers unable to obtain information or use other services through the banks’ online platforms.

When the two websites were accessed at around 12:30 pm today, notices stated that maintenance work was under way and that the websites would be back online soon. The banks apologised to customers for the inconvenience. However, repeated attempts to access the websites later were unsuccessful.

Bangladesh Bank website restored after 3-day shutdown over cyberattack fears

Attempts to contact Janata Bank’s acting managing director, Fayaz Alam, for comment were unsuccessful.

Concerns about possible cyberattacks on banks and other financial institutions have been growing over the past few days. Bangladesh Bank’s official website was taken offline last Thursday as a precaution. It was restored at 8:00 am today, Sunday, after three days.

The websites of Agrani Bank, IFIC Bank, Standard Islami Bank and SBAC Bank had also been taken offline during this period, but they are now operational.

However, internet banking and mobile banking transactions continued as normal over the past three days, causing no disruption to customers’ transactions.

Cybersecurity threat spreads worldwide, affecting Bangladesh too

Speaking to Prothom Alo today, Bangladesh Bank spokesperson Arif Hossain Khan said the website had been checked for possible vulnerabilities. The decision to take it offline was made amid fears of cyberattacks worldwide. As the risk has subsided, the website has been restored.

The internet and software are now essential for operating government services, banking, e-commerce, news outlets and various online platforms.

A large proportion of these websites rely on the PHP programming language. The recent discovery of two serious security vulnerabilities in PHP has raised global concerns about cybersecurity.

item.title: Mobilising grassroots to deliver new plastic recycling goals
item.description:
There have been a lot of public conversations and concerns often raised over the growing plastic pollution in the country. Finally, in August, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change introduced the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Guidelines on Plastic Waste Management.

This month the National Plastic Action Plan Partnership (NPAP) has been launched by the environment, forest and climate change ministry in collaboration with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the World Economic Forum's Global Plastic Action Partnership (GPAP).  These are certainly important steps to manage plastic waste and eliminate plastic pollution through unified national action.

In a country of more than 170 million people, plastic pollution cannot be tackled by the government alone. It is not realistic to expect the government to manage plastic waste across every village, town, and city. The only solution is for everyone to participate and contribute. The guidelines mark an important shift in how responsibility for plastic waste is shared.

Plastic pollution and responsible waste disposal

Sustainable progress will require collective action from producers, consumers, and local communities. By channeling producer funding into building and empowering community-based waste management systems, the EPR framework, if compliance is ensured, has the potential to strengthen grassroots recycling efforts and deliver lasting environmental impact.

Globally, there is now a growing acknowledgement that reducing plastic pollution requires collective responsibility. Every individual, institution, and sector has a role to play. This new framework will play a significant role in expanding waste collection and recycling infrastructure, formalising the informal waste collection sector and developing a circular economy of plastic waste.

Government agencies provide regulations and public infrastructure, but long-term sustainability requires civic ownership. Proper waste management is a shared societal duty; every household, shopkeeper, and community member generates waste and must play an active role in its lifecycle.

The framework holds producers, brand owners, and importers accountable for post-consumer waste, setting mandatory collection targets starting at 15 per cent and scaling up to 30 per cent. Under the new guidelines, waste being collected directly by municipal bodies cannot count toward a company’s compliance target. This obligates businesses, either individually or through collective Producer Responsibility Organizations (PROs), to build distinct, verifiable collection channels. Rather than duplicating infrastructure, producers should channel compliance capital straight into neighborhood-level systems.

So how do we ensure that everyone is engaged and actively contributing to tackling this growing crisis? Research shows that people are far more likely to adopt environmentally responsible habits when they see others around them doing the same.

In both urban and rural areas, communities and societies are organised around mosques, making it a powerful platform for awareness and collective action

We have often seen that there is not enough social pressure to act sustainably. It indicates that we have to build strong, motivated communities that are inspired to act and address this issue in their respective area.

When communities become confident, organised, and inspired, they can drive the kind of collective change that no policy alone can achieve. There are already examples of community actions funded by corporate brand owners that are making significant changes in our country. We need to fund more of such initiatives under the new framework.

We know that plastic pollution is not only a national challenge, it is a global crisis. If we can engage our educated youth in grassroots campaigns, community mobilisation, and waste management, it is not just beneficial for local communities—it opens pathways to professional opportunities with international relevance. Global initiatives increasingly prioritize community driven approaches, social norm shifts, and behavior change strategies as essential tools for tackling plastic pollution. These are the same skills young people can develop through grassroots environmental work in Bangladesh.

With this new framework, community based initiatives can be empowered and can play a highly influential and sustainable role. In both urban and rural areas, communities and societies are organised around mosques, making it a powerful platform for awareness and collective action.

One point we have to note that currently a large share of plastic bottles and other items that have post-consumer commercial value are being collected and processed, though the system needs to be formalized. The crisis is being exacerbated by the various food packaging and thin single use polyethene that have no post-consumer recycle value. Only community-based approaches can tackle this.

Having an active system for segregating, collecting and managing daily waste is a bigger part of building healthier and more resilient community. If communities are empowered with knowledge, training, and incentives under the new EPR rules, local youths are far more likely to participate because they will be the immediate beneficiaries.

A major obstacle to tackling plastic pollution is the country's limited waste management capacity. The EPR guidelines offer a practical pathway to address this gap by investing in community-led collection, sorting, and recycling networks. Combined with sustained local engagement, these efforts can foster greater public participation and encourage more responsible waste disposal practices.

However, the success of the EPR framework will ultimately depend on effective compliance and accountability mechanisms. One key concern has been already highlighted that a uniform compliance structure may disproportionately affect micro, cottage, and small enterprises, which often lack the resources available to larger companies. Future work can be on how these gaps can be minimised and made it more practical for all involved.

* Parvez Uddin Chowdhury is a development worker and climate enthusiast.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,227 as five die in 24 hours
item.description:
Five more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,227.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all five of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,123, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 104, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the five new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in the Chittagong division with two deaths. At the district level, one casualty each was recorded in Chittagong, Noakhali, Dhaka, Sunamganj, and Mymensingh.
A total of 1,280 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 221,164.
During the same period, 76 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 23,400.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 196,703 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 188,674 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Sexual abuse allegations at madrasas raise questions over oversight
item.description:
A series of allegations of sexual abuse involving students at madrasas across Bangladesh has raised questions about child protection, complaint mechanisms and institutional accountability, particularly in residential institutions where children live away from their families.
Recent cases in Gazipur, Kushtia, Chittagong, Pabna and Brahmanbaria have led to arrests and criminal proceedings against teachers and madrasa officials. Some cases involve allegations of repeated sexual abuse, while earlier incidents include the deaths of children.
The High Court has issued directives requiring educational institutions and workplaces to establish committees to prevent sexual harassment, receive complaints, investigate allegations and recommend appropriate action. However, reports of alleged abuse in both Alia and Qawmi madrasas have prompted questions about how effectively these safeguards are being implemented.
Alia madrasas operate under the supervision of government education authorities and the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board. Qawmi madrasas, by contrast, largely operate under their own education boards and management structures.
The distinction has renewed debate over who is responsible for monitoring individual institutions, ensuring that complaints are investigated and holding authorities accountable when allegations are ignored.
In recent weeks, cases have been filed and arrests made following allegations of sexual abuse involving children at Qawmi madrasas in Tongi and Gachha in Gazipur. In Banshkhali, Chittagong, a madrasa headmaster was arrested over allegations of repeatedly sexually abusing an eight-year-old student.
In Daulatpur, Kushtia, a Qawmi madrasa teacher was arrested following an allegation that he attempted to rape a nine-year-old student. A separate case involving an Alia-stream Dakhil madrasa teacher in Brahmanbaria also resulted in an arrest over the alleged rape of a female student.
These cases have drawn attention to the safety of students, particularly children living in residential institutions, and the availability of safe and effective channels for reporting abuse.
On October 20, an allegation of sexual harassment was raised against Mosleh Uddin, vice-principal of Qari Ul Quran International Madrasa in Madhya Auchpara, Tongi, Gazipur, involving a seven-year-old student.
The child's family alleged that the teacher kissed the child inappropriately and threatened physical punishment if the incident was disclosed. After the child's father filed a case, police arrested the accused. A court subsequently ordered that he be sent to jail.
In Pakuria village under Pragpur Union in Daulatpur upazila, Kushtia, Sayeed Hossain, also known as Nannu, a teacher at Darul Abrar Madrasa, was accused of attempting to rape a nine-year-old third-grade student.
The child's mother filed a case on October 20. The teacher was arrested and subsequently sent to jail.
In Gazipur, police arrested teacher Oliullah Islam and madrasa director Mohammad Mizan following allegations that an eight-year-old residential student at Darul Hedaya Qawmi Madrasa in the Kalmeswar area under Gachha police station had been repeatedly sexually abused. Both were sent to jail on October 23.
According to the case statement, the child's family had reported the alleged abuse to the madrasa authorities, but no action was taken. The family also alleged that attempts were made to cover up the incident.
Three people were named as accused in the case, two of whom had been arrested, according to the report.
In Banshkhali, Chittagong, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested madrasa headmaster Muhammad Ramiz Uddin on August 3 over allegations of repeatedly sexually abusing an eight-year-old student.
He was arrested in the Bairag area near China Road, close to the Karnaphuli Tunnel in Anwara.
The child studied at Darussunnah Khairia Madrasa in Paschim Chechuria Ghonapara, Bailchhari Union, Banshkhali.
According to the case statement, the teacher allegedly took the child to a washroom and abused the student repeatedly, threatening the child to ensure silence. The alleged abuse was said to have continued from the time the child enrolled at the institution.
After the madrasa closed on July 23, another alleged incident reportedly took place in a classroom on the second floor of the orphanage's Hifz department, where students memorise the Quran.
The child's father filed a case on July 29 under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
Earlier incidents have also raised concerns about the safety of children in Qawmi madrasas.
In June 2019, a teacher named Hafizur Rahman was arrested in Sharsha, Jessore, over allegations that he attempted to sexually assault and subsequently murdered 12-year-old student. Police said the child was killed after the alleged attempt to sexually assault him failed. The teacher was arrested at a Qawmi madrasa in Dighalia, Khulna.
In March 2022, three teachers were arrested after the body of an eight-year-old student was found with his throat slit at a Qawmi madrasa in Boalkhali, Chittagong.
More recently, in Pabna Sadar upazila, Md Abu Yusuf, a teacher and director of Nure Madina Women's Qawmi Madrasa in Dari Bhaudanga, Bharara Union, was accused of sexually abusing and attempting to rape a student.
Local residents detained him on October 22 and handed him over to police. The following day, an angry crowd vandalised the madrasa and set it on fire.
Allegations of sexual offences have also emerged at Alia-stream institutions.
In Kasba, Brahmanbaria, Abul Bashar, a mathematics teacher at a Dakhil madrasa, was accused of raping a sixth-grade student. A medical examination reportedly found that the student was three months pregnant.
The teacher was arrested, and the student's father filed a case under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. The student alleged that the teacher had threatened to kill her if she disclosed the incident.
According to data from Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), 118 children were victims of rape, and 46 were victims of attempted rape in Bangladesh between January and May 20, 2026.
Data compiled by France-based human rights organisation JusticeMakers Bangladesh in France (JMBF) documented 171 victims across 131 incidents of sexual violence against boys between January and September 2026.
Of those incidents, 72 occurred in madrasas and involved 109 boys. The organisation recorded allegations against 81 madrasa teachers in 65 of the cases.
JMBF's data do not distinguish between Qawmi and Alia madrasas. ASK's figures, meanwhile, cover violence against children nationwide rather than incidents specifically involving madrasa students.
As a result, the available figures do not establish the total number of sexual abuse cases occurring in madrasas or allow a direct comparison between the two education systems.
Human rights organisations in Bangladesh monitor incidents of rape and other forms of violence largely through media reports and other available information. However, they do not maintain separate national statistics categorised by educational institution.
Consequently, there is no comprehensive monthly or annual count of rape cases specifically involving students at madrasas.
ASK recorded 641 incidents of rape involving women and children across Bangladesh between January and July 2026. The figure included 400 cases involving women and 241 involving children.
Abu Ahmed Faizul Kabir, a senior coordinator at ASK, told Bangla Tribune that the organisation did not categorise its records by institution and therefore could not provide separate figures for madrasas.
"We do not maintain records categorised by institution; therefore, there are no separate figures for madrasas. However, our observations suggest that incidents of rape and sexual harassment occur in educational institutions, including madrasas," he said.
He added that this did not mean such incidents were absent from other types of educational institutions. ASK had also observed cases in which boys were raped or sexually abused in madrasas, he said.
The absence of institution-specific data makes it difficult to assess the scale of the problem in madrasas, identify patterns and determine whether existing preventive measures are working.
On May 14, 2009, the High Court Division issued landmark directives aimed at preventing sexual harassment in workplaces and educational institutions.
The guidelines called for complaints committees to be established in public and private educational institutions and workplaces. The committees are required to be headed by a woman and include at least two members from outside the institution or organisation.
The directives were intended to remain in force until a separate law on sexual harassment was enacted.
The committees' responsibilities extend beyond receiving complaints. They are expected to examine allegations, conduct investigations and recommend appropriate action. Where a complaint is substantiated, the relevant authorities are required to take action in accordance with applicable rules.
However, the effectiveness of the system depends not only on establishing committees but also on ensuring that they are functional, accessible to students and capable of investigating complaints impartially.
Recent allegations involving madrasa students have raised questions about whether the directives are being implemented effectively, particularly in residential institutions.
On April 16, 2019, the Directorate of Madrasa Education issued a notice calling for committees to be formed to prevent sexual harassment and for oversight to be strengthened. On April 30 that year, the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board issued a similar directive to its affiliated institutions.
Alia-stream madrasas operate within a government-supervised framework involving the Bangladesh Madrasa Education Board and relevant education authorities.
Qawmi madrasas, however, generally operate under independent education boards and management structures.
Al-Haiatul Ulya Lil-Jamiatil Qawmia Bangladesh, which brings together six Qawmi madrasa education boards, coordinates the recognition of Dawra-e-Hadith (Takmil) certificates and related academic activities.
Its role does not, however, extend to routine supervision of every individual madrasa or the direct investigation of allegations of sexual abuse at those institutions.
This distinction raises questions about the mechanisms available to monitor individual Qawmi madrasas, receive complaints from students and guardians, and ensure that allegations are referred to the appropriate authorities.
The two streams of madrasas should not be assumed to operate under identical administrative arrangements. Nevertheless, regardless of an institution's management structure, allegations of criminal conduct must be addressed under the applicable law.
Zahid Hasan Fahad, a Supreme Court lawyer and joint secretary of the human rights organisation Rise for Rights Foundation, told Bangla Tribune that the allegations in the Tongi case would have to be established through the legal process.
However, he said the allegation that madrasa authorities had failed to act after being informed of the incident warranted particular attention.
"If this allegation proves true, it suggests that the institution lacks an effective sexual harassment prevention committee, as mandated by the High Court," he said.
He described the matter as particularly sensitive because the institution caters to young children.
"If it is established that complaints were ignored or directives were disregarded, then not only the accused individual but also the institution and its head must be brought under the purview of the law," he said.
Fahad said the 2009 High Court ruling required educational institutions and workplaces across the country to establish committees to prevent sexual harassment. Yet, many institutions had either failed to form such committees or had committees that were ineffective, he said.
He added that those responsible should be held accountable if oversight of the directives' implementation was found to be inadequate.
Depending on the circumstances and available evidence, he said, there could also be grounds for initiating contempt of court proceedings.
Muhammad Mozammel Hossain Khan, director of administration and finance at the Directorate of Madrasa Education, told Bangla Tribune that the directorate regularly issued instructions aimed at preventing sexual abuse in madrasas.
The instructions included disseminating relevant guidance and holding periodic meetings with guardians to discuss the issue. Monitoring at the upazila level was carried out through upazila secondary education officers, he said.
However, the directorate did not have its own dedicated field-level monitoring mechanism, he added.
Mozammel said reports of such incidents had increased recently and that monitoring needed to be strengthened.
"We will work on this and place greater emphasis on the implementation of these directives," he said.
The Directorate of Madrasa Education said Alia madrasas were monitored at the field level by officials of the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education, as the Directorate of Madrasa Education did not have its own dedicated field-level staff.
Maulana Bahauddin Zakaria, vice-president of Befaqul Madarisil Arabia Bangladesh and senior joint secretary general of Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh, said Qawmi madrasas operated under their own curricula and management systems.
Each madrasa had its own committee, and teachers were accountable to that committee, he told Bangla Tribune.
"I am not certain to what extent the High Court's directives apply to Qawmi madrasas. Nevertheless, even when isolated untoward incidents occur, the madrasa boards and authorities remain vigilant and play a proactive role," he said.
He added that madrasa authorities took action against individuals involved in wrongdoing, although such action often went unreported.
A professor in the Department of Arabic Language and Literature at Government Madrasa-e-Alia told Bangla Tribune that government educational institutions had committees to address drug abuse and sexual harassment.
He said similar committees should be established at private educational institutions and made fully functional.
Regular monitoring was also necessary to ensure that the committees could perform their duties effectively, he added.
Children may be reluctant to report sexual abuse because of fear, shame or social pressure. These barriers can be particularly difficult for students at residential madrasas, who live away from their families and may depend on teachers and administrators for their daily needs.
In the Gachha case in Gazipur, the child's family alleged that the madrasa authorities failed to act after being informed of the alleged abuse. Similar allegations have also appeared in a report by BBC Bangla.
The allegations must be established through an impartial investigation. However, claims that complaints were ignored highlight the need for reporting mechanisms that children and guardians can access without fear of retaliation.
Removing an accused teacher from an institution, on its own, is not enough to address an allegation. Authorities must ensure an impartial investigation, take appropriate legal action where warranted and put safeguards in place to prevent further abuse.
Students should be able to report concerns to a trusted adult or an independent authority, particularly when the person accused of abuse holds a position of power within the institution.
Those concerned with child protection say madrasas should establish or activate complaints committees and clearly communicate the names of committee members and their contact details to students and guardians.
Institutions should also provide safe and confidential channels for reporting abuse, including alternative ways to lodge complaints when a student cannot approach the institution's management directly.
When allegations are received, authorities should ensure impartial investigations, protect the confidentiality of complainants and take appropriate legal measures. Complaints should be documented, and residential madrasas should be subject to regular inspections.
Institutions must also be held accountable for attempts to intimidate complainants, suppress reports or shield accused individuals from investigation.
Teachers, students and guardians should receive guidance on child protection, recognising inappropriate behaviour and reporting concerns.
The responsibilities of education boards, government departments and madrasa management committees should be clearly defined for both Qawmi and Alia institutions. Effective oversight requires more than issuing directives or formally establishing committees: reporting channels must work, allegations must be investigated fairly, and those responsible for neglecting their duties must be held accountable.
Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh has said that six Qawmi madrasa education boards and institutions under their jurisdiction have been instructed to form or activate student protection committees to prevent abuse and immoral conduct.
In a statement sent to the media on Saturday night, the organisation's joint secretary general, Maulana Azizul Haque Islamabadi, said allegations of student abuse or unethical behaviour must be investigated and reports submitted within a maximum of seven days.
The statement also said the madrasa boards had been directed to establish monitoring cells and hotlines through which complaints could be reported.
Hefazat Ameer Allama Shah Muhibbullah Babunagari and Secretary General Allama Sajedur Rahman said Al-Haiatul Ulya Lil-Jamiatil Qawmia Bangladesh had issued the instructions on September 19.
The leaders said child abuse and other forms of misconduct in educational institutions were unacceptable, but stressed that people must not take the law into their own hands.
They called for fair investigations and appropriate action through administrative and legal channels to maintain law and order.
Describing child sexual abuse as a longstanding social problem, the leaders said it was not confined to any one community or type of institution, noting that abuse could occur in schools, madrasas and other settings.
They warned that institutions could face suspension or cancellation of affiliation if they failed to establish student protection committees, allowed committees to remain inactive or failed to act on complaints.
The statement also stressed that children's safety and emotional well-being must be prioritised. It called on schools and madrasas to follow the instructions issued by their respective authorities and warned that those found guilty of misconduct should face both institutional and legal consequences.
The leaders said there would be no compromise in dealing with such cases, emphasising the responsibility of educational institutions to provide children with a safe environment for learning and development.
Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Hossain, also known as Kaikobad, described the reported incidents as "very sad and shameful".
He made the remarks on Saturday morning after the triennial council session of the Bangladesh National Imam Association in Agargaon, Dhaka.
"I have noticed that such incidents in the country are very sad and shameful. I believe this thing will not happen in future. We will do what is necessary in that regard," he said.
The minister added that imams had been instructed to raise awareness to help prevent such acts in religious institutions, including madrasas.

item.title: Offices reopen after five-day holiday
item.description:
Government, semi-government and autonomous offices across the country reopened on Sunday after a five-day holiday for Durga Puja and the weekend.
Banks, insurance companies, the stock market and private-sector establishments also resumed operations.
According to the official holiday calendar, October 20 was a holiday by executive order for Durga Puja (Maha Navami), followed by a public holiday on October 21 for Vijaya Dashami. Thursday, October 22, was also declared a holiday by executive order.
The holidays were followed by the regular weekend on Friday and Saturday, October 23 and 24, keeping offices and courts closed for five consecutive days.
With the holidays over, traffic and commuter numbers increased on the capital’s streets from Sunday morning as people returned to work.
Traffic congestion was reported in several areas, including Badda, Rampura, Mohakhali, Farmgate, Shahbagh and Tejgaon.
Rafiqul Islam, deputy commissioner of the Tejgaon Traffic Division, said the volume of people and vehicles had increased as offices reopened after the extended break.
He added that although traffic congestion occurred earlier in the morning, the situation had since returned to normal.

item.description:

item.title: HSBC-BGMEA to promote manufacturing capabilities in BD apparel roadshow in Hong Kong
item.description:
The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited in Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in collaboration with the Consulate General of Bangladesh in Hong Kong, is organizing “Bangladesh Apparel Roadshow” in Hong Kong on October 28 at the Island Shangri-La, Hong Kong.
The initiative will bring together global buyers, sourcing partners and industry stakeholders to showcase Bangladesh’s evolving apparel manufacturing capabilities, including product diversification, technical apparel, innovation and sustainable manufacturing.
As one of the world’s leading apparel-exporting countries, Bangladesh continues to advance its position in the global value chain.
Against the backdrop of evolving global sourcing strategies and changing market dynamics, the roadshow will provide a platform to highlight the sector’s expanding capabilities and explore opportunities for deeper international trade and collaboration.
The program will feature presentations on Bangladesh’s apparel capabilities, discussions on the global retail outlook and emerging sourcing trends, a panel discussion, and an apparel showcase highlighting innovation and technical apparel.
Senior officials from the HSBC Hong Kong team including Oliver T Jones, head of global network banking, Hong Kong, amongst many others will participate in the discussions.
The event will facilitate engagement between international buyers and industry stakeholders, supporting dialogue on emerging opportunities, and the evolving requirements of global apparel supply chains.
Through its international network, global trade expertise and longstanding presence in Bangladesh, HSBC continues supporting businesses in navigating international markets and pursue cross-border growth opportunities.
The roadshow reflects the bank’s commitment to facilitating international business connections and supporting Bangladesh’s participation in global trade.
BGMEA, as the apex trade body representing Bangladesh’s apparel manufacturers and exporters, brings industry expertise and representation to the initiative.
The collaboration also underscores the importance of strengthening international engagement to support the sector’s diversification, competitiveness and long-term growth.
Md Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO, HSBC Bangladesh, and Mahmud Hasan Khan, president, BGMEA, will co-host the event.

item.title: Gold prices cut by Tk3,324 per bhori in Bangladesh
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) on Sunday cut gold prices by Tk3,324 per bhori, setting the price of 22-carat gold at Tk220,858, including valued added tax (VAT).
The revised prices came into effect at 10am on Sunday, according to a Bajus press release.
The organisation said it lowered gold prices following a decline in the price of pure gold in the local market.
Under the new rates, 21-carat gold will cost Tk210,943 per bhori, 18-carat gold Tk181,200 and traditional-method gold Tk148,016.
Bajus said making charges will apply depending on the design of the jewellery. As VAT is included in the selling prices of gold and silver ornaments, jewellers cannot collect it separately from customers.
For jewellery exchanges, 12% will be deducted from the price, excluding making charges and stones, while 18% will be deducted for purchases. VAT cannot be deducted separately in exchange and purchase transactions, the association said.
The revised prices will remain effective at all jewellery establishments until further notice.
Before Sunday's adjustment, Bajus last revised gold prices on October 23, slashing Tk2,158 per bhori to set the price of 22-carat gold at Tk224,182, including VAT.
At the time, 21-carat gold was priced at Tk214,093 per bhori, 18-carat gold at Tk183,883 and traditional-method gold at Tk150,232.
With Sunday's adjustment, gold prices have been revised 126 times in the domestic market so far this year. Prices have been raised 60 times, lowered 65 times, and adjusted once for VAT.
Meanwhile, silver prices remained unchanged in the domestic market.
Including VAT, 22-carat silver is selling at Tk3,849 per bhori, 21-carat silver at Tk3,674, 18-carat silver at Tk3,149 and traditional-method silver at Tk2,391.
Silver prices have been revised 76 times so far this year, with 36 increases and 40 decreases.

item.title: IGP: 27 police personnel sent to jail over drug links in two months
item.description:
A total of 27 police personnel have been sent to jail over alleged involvement in drug-related activities in the past two months, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir has said.
Emphasizing the need to clean up the police force first to eliminate drugs, he called on the public to help law enforcement agencies by providing information, reports Bangla Tribune.
He made the comments while addressing a community policing rally against drugs, terrorism, extortion, corruption, juvenile gangs and extremism at the Bagerhat Police Lines auditorium on Sunday afternoon.
The IGP stressed that the police force must first cleanse itself before tackling drugs in the country. He also urged the public to provide the police with necessary information to make anti-drug operations successful.
Expressing concern over the spread of drugs across the country, Ali Hossain Fakir said he believed drug dens had been established in various areas under government patronage over the past 17 years. The police and the public must work together to dismantle these networks, he added.
Highlighting a shortage of police personnel, the IGP said the country currently had around 215,000 police members. Although the government planned to recruit 20,000 personnel this year, there was insufficient infrastructure to train such a large number at once.
He said new training centres were needed and called on everyone to work together to ensure the country's development and prosperity.
The IGP also said special committees had been formed, comprising upazila nirbahi officers (UNOs) and officers-in-charge (OCs) of police stations, to curb juvenile gang activities.
The committees will operate from the district to the union level. He expressed hope that information provided by local residents would help identify and prevent criminal activities involving juveniles.
Announcing plans to establish a specialised unit to combat cybercrime, the police chief said it would work to prevent the spread of rumours online and incidents of mob violence.
Identifying unemployment as one of the key reasons young people become involved in crime, Ali Hossain Fakir said around 2.7 million people in the country face unemployment every year.
He stressed the need to create jobs for this working-age population, adding that new employment opportunities would not emerge unless businesses increased investment.
Asked about former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's return to Bangladesh, the IGP said neither the administration nor community police had any concern about who would or would not return to the country.

item.title: Salahuddin: Next general election to be held under caretaker govt
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday said the next general election will be held under a caretaker government system.
“The next general election will be held under a caretaker government,” he made the remarks at a press briefing at the Ministry of Home Affairs following the successful and peaceful celebration of Durga Puja.
Emphasizing the government’s position on restoring the caretaker government system, he said that there was political consensus on holding the next general election under a caretaker administration.
He indicated that the caretaker government system would be restored and maintained through constitutional amendments in Parliament.
The home minister also addressed questions about alleged political coordination between the banned Awami League and Jamaat-e-Islami aimed at overthrowing the government, saying the government had already made its position clear on the matter.

item.title: Kishoreganj-Dhaka bus services halted over transport owners’ dispute
item.description:
Bus services on the Kishoreganj-Dhaka route have been suspended indefinitely since Sunday morning following a dispute between transport owners in Kishoreganj and Dhaka, causing suffering for commuters.
The Kishoreganj District Road Transport Owners’ Association announced the suspension, halting all private bus services on the route.
Association leaders said the newly formed committee took an initiative to improve passenger services by replacing old buses with new ones after assuming responsibility. Following discussions, transport owners in Dhaka also agreed to the proposal.
However, while Kishoreganj owners replaced their old buses with new ones, their Dhaka counterparts did not replace their outdated vehicles and instead added two more buses to the route, they said.
Tensions mounted between the two factions over the issue, culminating in a sharp dispute on Saturday.
Following the dispute, the Kishoreganj association suspended all private bus services on the Kishoreganj-Mohakhali route from Sunday morning.
The suspension left passengers travelling between Kishoreganj and Dhaka facing considerable inconvenience.

item.title: Infantino says he has overwhelming support ahead of FIFA presidential election
item.description:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino has claimed that he enjoys the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of the football community despite facing criticism over his failed proposal to sell stakes in World Cup profits.
Infantino is seeking re-election for a final term next year, amid calls from some quarters for him to step down following the controversial plan.
His proposal to sell shares in World Cup profits through a commercial subsidiary angered football officials in Europe, North America and Asia.
However, in an interview with the BBC released on Saturday during the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, Infantino dismissed calls for his resignation.
"Well, you know, I was elected by 211 member associations from all over the world," Infantino said.
"I think what is important is that in an organization like FIFA there can be different views, different points of view.
"But if we are serious about democracy, about the democratic process, about believing that everyone has the same vote and the same voice all over the world, that football belongs to everyone, if we are serious about that, then we need to respect as well the views of the vast, vast majority," he added.
Infantino is seeking a final term in office in the election scheduled for March. The deadline for rival candidates to enter the race is November 18.
His latest remarks came after he apologised to FIFA's ruling council last week for what he described as "mistakes" in his secretive investment plan involving the World Cup.
Despite the apology, European delegates said they left the meeting disappointed, citing what they considered a lack of clarity over the proposal.
On Friday, the Asian Football Confederation endorsed Infantino for another term, marking an apparent shift from its position two months earlier, when it criticised him for what it called a breach of trust.

item.title: Apologetic Alvarez fires Atletico to win against Deportivo
item.description:
Julian Alvarez continued on his road to redemption by scoring as Atletico Madrid beat Deportivo La Coruna 1-0 on Saturday, closing the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to two points, and apologising to the club's supporters for trying to leave this summer.
Diego Simeone's side are second, with champions Barca hosting Real Madrid, third, in the Clasico at Camp Nou on Sunday.
Alvarez netted for the second consecutive game, having grabbed his first of the season in Atletico's 1-1 Champions League draw at Stuttgart in midweek.
Atletico supporters hounded Alvarez during his first appearances this season after he tried to force his way out of the club in the summer, but the tension has gradually cooled.
After the game Alvarez apologised to the fans and said it was a "mistake" on his part.
"I understand people's anger, I would have been angry too," Alvarez told Movistar.
Simeone was pleased that the Argentina international had apologised.
"It's not easy to say sorry, I'm very happy for him, he will feel very at peace," said the coach.
"We need him. If the club wants to reach where the fans dream, we need a very good Julian Alvarez."
Atletico goalkeeper Jan Oblak believes Alvarez will earn the love of supporters again, over the weeks ahead.
"I'm happy for him, he's giving the best of himself, a lot of effort, and I'm sure bit by bit he'll win over the fans again," Oblak told Movistar.
"He's a great player, he's shown it already and he's on the road to showing it again -- we need him in the best form possible."
Home fans at the Metropolitano stadium directed a few whistles at the team in general after a slow start, with Deportivo having the best chance of the first half.
Oblak saved well from Lorenzo Amatucci, while at the other end Simeone's side lacked spark.
Early in the second half Alvarez found the breakthrough.
Alejandro Grimaldo fired in a dangerous low pass towards the far post, where the Argentina international turned it over the line.
Alvarez came close to a second after a slick team move, with Alex Baena slipping him in, but Depor goalkeeper Leo Roman saved the striker's attempted lob with his face.
The former Manchester City striker looked much closer to his best form in this outing after struggling with some fitness problems earlier in the campaign.
After apologising to Atletico's fans for trying to depart this summer, Alvarez said he was slowly improving.
"I'm starting to feel good... I'm grateful to all my teammates because they've supported me. They've really stuck by me throughout this whole time," said Alvarez.
"I'm working to improve. I've felt better in these last few matches."
Deportivo forward Kevin Sanchez spurned two fine chances in stoppage time.
"In the first half we played quite badly, in the second better but then we dipped at the end again," added Oblak. "We had a bit of luck."
- Mikautadze strikes late -
Earlier, Georges Mikautadze snatched a late 2-1 win for Villarreal in a derby clash against Valencia, who had midfielder Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men.
The Yellow Submarine came from behind to triumph, climbing into mid-table and leaving Javier Aguirre's Los Che 19th, in the relegation zone.
Pepelu sent Valencia ahead from the penalty spot in the first half before American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level at Mestalla stadium after 69 minutes.
Inigo Perez's Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit Jose Gaya in the face with his elbow.
However, English midfielder Elliott, on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent.
Villarreal striker Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.

item.title: This simple habit can end your child’s endless demands
item.description:
Tantrums are rarely just misbehavior. Understanding what lies behind them is the first step to handling them well.
Children often cannot express their wants and feelings properly. When they don’t get something, they cry or dig in their heels. The same behavior can also stem from a bid for parents’ attention or from tiredness, hunger, or lack of sleep. Before trying to manage a child’s tantrums, parents should therefore try to understand the cause. Follow a few simple principles, and you will find that needless demands fall away considerably.
When a child is being stubborn, don’t silence them with scolding or shouting. That can make matters worse. Listen calmly instead, and try to understand why they are behaving this way.
Children calm down faster when someone listens to them. Over time, they start using words for big feelings instead of tears.
Don’t grant every request just to stop a child from crying. This can give them the idea that being stubborn gets them what they want. Explain in simple language what is necessary and what is not.
Once you have said no to something, don’t change your decision, however much the child cries.
Children often make demands to win their parents’ attention. Set aside some time each day to play with your child, talk with them, and join in the activities they enjoy. During this time, keep your phone away and give them your full attention. This supports their emotional development and strengthens your bond with them. On weekends, you could also take your child out somewhere.
When a child calmly expresses a need instead of being stubborn, praise them. Encourage and reward even small good deeds. This helps them see that speaking calmly and being patient are good behavior, and they will cut down needless demands by themselves.
Create age-appropriate rules for situations such as shopping, outings, visits to relatives, and playtime, and build the habit of following them. Encourage other family members to take part in observing these rules too.
However, never resort to hitting, humiliating, or frightening a child in the name of discipline. Teach the right behavior through love and empathy.
Excessive use of mobile phones or television can also make children stubborn. Set screen limits according to age, and encourage creative activities such as sports, drawing, and reading storybooks.
When dealing with a child’s tantrums, hitting, shouting, and scare tactics have no place. Patience, empathy, and consistent behavior matter most. Parents should understand the reason behind each of their child’s actions and give appropriate guidance when needed.
The goal is not to crush a child’s stubbornness. A parent’s main responsibility is to teach the child to control their emotions and strike a balance between what they want and what they can have.

item.title: Blackheads aren’t dirt! The real reason will surprise you
item.description:
Acne, blackheads, and whiteheads are among the most common skin problems. In medical terms, blackheads and whiteheads are known as “comedones.”
Although they look similar, dermatologists say they differ in type and cause. The problem begins when sebum (excess oil) and dead skin cells get trapped in the hair follicles. To treat them properly, however, it is essential to understand how they differ.
Blackheads: In this case, the opening of the pore stays open.
As a result, the oil and dead cells trapped inside come into contact with the air and undergo a chemical reaction (oxidation), turning black. This is not caused by dirt or dust from outside but by a chemical change in the oil itself.
Whiteheads: Here, the opening of the pore is covered by a thin layer of skin. Because air cannot get inside, no oxidation occurs, and the contents appear as white or pale yellowish bumps.
Since the pore opening is closed, bacterial infection can develop in it, which may later turn into painful acne.
According to dermatologists, picking at these blemishes with fingernails or squeezing them can cause skin infections and permanent pitted scars.

item.title: Bangladesh's largest renewable energy festival to return for 2nd time
item.description:
Meeting the country's growing electricity demand while ensuring national energy security now demands the effective utilization and strengthening of indigenous and renewable resources.
Against this backdrop, the three-day 'Renewable Energy Fest 2026' is set to take place from 26 to 28 October 2026 at the Central Playground of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (Buet) in Dhaka, charting a roadmap for a sustainable, inclusive, and just energy future.
This is the second edition of the country's only and largest renewable energy festival to be held in the capital.
The festival will be inaugurated on 27 October by Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku, Minister of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources.
Also in attendance will be Prof Ekramul Haq, vice-chancellor of Buet, and Farah Kabir, country director of ActionAid Bangladesh, among other distinguished guests.
Additionally, two Buet professors will deliver keynote addresses at the Energy Talks on the first and second days, and Prof Mamun Ahmed, chairman of the University Grants Commission (UGC), will grace the closing ceremony.
Themed 'A Just, Inclusive and Green Energy Transition', the festival will feature an Energy Justice Assembly, Innovation and Technology Fair, Investment and Business Networking, a dedicated platform for Women, Youth and Grassroots Organizations, and High-Level Policy Dialogue.
To overcome challenges and transform the expansion of renewable energy into a sustainable national movement, the festival is being jointly organized by ActionAid Bangladesh, Buet, JETnet-BD, and Buet's Institute of Energy and Sustainable Development (IESD).
The first day of the festival, 26 October, will begin with 'Power to the People: Energy Justice Assembly'.
Women, youth, workers, and marginalized communities affected by climate change will come together at this assembly to present their daily struggles, local solutions to the crisis, and demands for energy rights directly to policymakers.
Following the formal inauguration on 27 October, the main festival exhibition will commence.
It will feature the 'Innovation Fair' and 'Technology Fair', where domestic innovators and corporate entities will showcase their latest renewable energy technologies and services.
To connect innovation with mainstream investment, an 'Innovation-to-Impact Marketplace' will be held, where young entrepreneurs and startups will present their business models to investors and banks, with the most promising ventures receiving seed funding.
On 28 October, the closing day of the festival, multiple high-level parallel dialogue sessions and plenary sessions will be held with consideration for national and regional contexts.
Detailed discussions will take place on the current state of Bangladesh's energy policy, ensuring social and environmental safeguards, and promoting good governance.
At the closing ceremony, innovators, young leaders, and partner organizations that have made special contributions to the renewable energy sector will be recognized and awarded.
Speaking about the objectives of the festival, Farah Kabir, country director of ActionAid Bangladesh, said: "Meeting the national solar power generation target by 2030 requires more than technological advancement; it demands human dignity, social justice, and a sense of collective responsibility. We believe the 'Renewable Energy Fest 2026' will serve as a powerful catalyst for that coordinated effort. With the collective participation of all, Bangladesh will move steadily towards a safe, green, and self-sufficient energy future, that is the core promise of this festival."
